candidates.original_title: The use of category and exemplar knowledge in the solution of anchoring tasks
candidates.description: An anchor selectively increases the accessibility of anchor-consistent knowledge, measured by faster lexical decision responses to anchor-consistent words following a comparative judgment.
candidates.citation_sentence: the one candidate test that we could identify in the literature to provide such a 'signature test' was the one described in Mussweiler and Strack (2000a, Studies 1 & 2), and evaluated in the present manuscript.
candidates.notes: Conceptual replication using Continuous IDentification (CID) task instead of Lexical Decision Task (LDT); temperature domain only.

candidates.original_title: The use of category and exemplar knowledge in the solution of anchoring tasks
candidates.description: A high temperature anchor increases accessibility of summer-related words and a low temperature anchor increases accessibility of winter-related words in a subsequent accessibility task.
candidates.citation_sentence: Five experiments followed the logic of [41], testing whether anchor-consistent concepts were selectively more accessible following an initial comparison question.
candidates.notes: Experiment 5 used a Continuous IDentification task as an alternative, conceptual test of the result and found no evidence of selective accessibility.

candidates.original_title: The use of category and exemplar knowledge in the solution of anchoring tasks
candidates.description: A high temperature anchor increases accessibility of summer-related words and a low temperature anchor increases accessibility of winter-related words in a subsequent lexical decision task.
candidates.citation_sentence: Experiments 1 and 2 are large-sample (at least relative to the original sample sizes) replications of Studies 1 and 2 from [41], which are the studies using the proposed 'signature test' that are closest to prototypical anchoring studies. This is in line with the procedure of Mussweiler and Strack (2000a, Study 2), who gave their participants four 'practice experiments'.
candidates.notes: Experiment 1 replicated Study 1 using UK participants and English materials; the authors explicitly report failing to replicate the selective-accessibility result. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
